findings.message: The new Owner-line regex only takes an address that follows a boundary character (`(?:^|[\s<(\[`"':*_])`). `^` has no `m` flag, so it can only match at the very start of the header, and the `**` of `**Owner:**` has already been used up by the time the boundary is tested. So an address written straight after the label, with no space, is no longer found. The old regex matched it. The domain part also ends in `\.[A-Za-z]{2,}` with no end anchor, so the match backs off and returns a shorter, different address. That is the 'cut down to a different address' defect the final pass says it fixed. The same regex is copied in plugins/amax/scripts/read-specclaw.mjs:70. Fix: let the boundary also be the end of the `**Owner:**` label, and require a non-address character or end of line after the domain. Add these cases to the owner-092 AC-2 table.
findings.scenario: Example 1: change.md header `**Owner:**nimal@lumenlabs.test` gives owner = null, so the sync falls back to the git author and assigns the wrong person. Example 2: `**Owner:** a@lumen.dev1` gives `a@lumen.dev`, which is a different address and resolves to whoever owns it.

findings.message: The 'owner frozen' rule now exists twice: `ownerFrozen` in JS (still used by `repoOwnerStale`) and `ownerFrozenSql` in SQL (used by `upsertSpecProposal`). The only link between them is a comment. They agree today, but if one changes alone, the pre-check that decides whether to rewrite and the write itself will disagree. Fix: build both from one definition, or add a table test that checks they give the same answer.

The unreadable-state.json skip used to run after the 091 AC-2 key check (a branch taking over a key the default branch holds). It now runs before it, through `skipReason`. A record that is both unreadable and in conflict is now reported as 'state.json unreadable' rather than as the key conflict. Both are skips, but the Repo sync card and needsReview reasons now differ from 091's order. Either keep the old order or say in the README that the order changed.

`proposeCreate` checks agent-first before it checks the viewer's per-project `delivery:proposal:create` permission. The refusal includes the project's `repo_url`. Because of that order, a person who can't add proposals to the project still sees its linked repo URL, where before they got "you can't add proposals to <name>". Fix: move the agent-first refusal below the `can(v, "delivery:proposal:create", { projectId })` check, so only people who could otherwise create a proposal there see the repo.
findings.scenario: A viewer with no proposal-create scope on HRI (agent-first, repo github.com/example/hr-intranet) asks chat to add a proposal to HRI → the card is refused with "HRI's proposals come from its repo (github.com/example/hr-intranet)…" instead of "you can't add proposals to HR Intranet".
